output:
Technically yes, but I'd recommend against it unless nobody outside your team has run the app yet. The rules file calls the identifier permanent, so changing it means overriding that rule on purpose, and that's your call.

**What a rename breaks for existing installs:**
- **Accessibility permission:** macOS ties the grant to the bundle ID, so every existing user would have to re-grant it. For a dictation app that likely means it silently stops working until they notice.
- **Sparkle updates:** Sparkle generally expects an update to have the same bundle ID as the installed app. Existing users may not be able to auto-update to the renamed build, so they'd have to reinstall manually. Verify this against your Sparkle version before relying on it.
- **Local data:** the UserDefaults domain, Keychain items, Application Support and cache folders, and login-item registration are all keyed to the ID. Settings would reset unless you write a migration.

**What doesn't change:** the Sparkle EdDSA key is independent of the bundle ID, so there's no reason to touch it. The rename also doesn't require `codesign --deep`. Nested code still needs signing inside-out with the new identifier.

**Recommendation:**
- If `is.waiwai.dictation` has shipped to real users or beta testers, keep it. Users never see the bundle ID, so you can still launch as OpenRamble by changing the display name (`CFBundleName` / `CFBundleDisplayName`), the app filename, and the marketing material.
- If it has never been distributed beyond your own machines, the rename is cheap now and expensive later. In that case, do it before launch and update the rules file, `docs/release.md`, and `AGENTS.md` so the "permanent" invariant points at the new ID.

**If you go ahead,** the checklist is:
- Change the ID in the Info.plist and build settings.
- Update the entitlements and any provisioning or notarization profiles.
- Update the Sparkle appcast and feed config.
- Update the URL schemes and any hardcoded `is.waiwai.dictation` strings.
- Re-sign everything from the inside out.
- Test a clean install on a machine that has never had the app.

Has the current ID shipped to anyone outside the team? That decides which path to take.
